connections.note: Graves names VFA-11 and Warning Area W-72 in sworn testimony as the locus of the encounters and the near-midair.

desc: The squadron whose 2014-2015 encounters turned UAP from a single spectacular incident into a documented, repeated flight-safety problem. Ryan Graves testified that 'In 2014, I was near Virginia Beach as part of VFA-11, a Navy Fighter/Attack Squadron made up of F/A-18F Super Hornets,' and that after the fleet's upgrade to the APG-79 AESA radar the squadron 'began witnessing advanced UAP demonstrating complex maneuvers on a regular basis.' The defining event occurred in Warning Area W-72 ten miles east of Virginia Beach, where a pilot saw 'a dark gray cube inside of a clear sphere - motionless against the wind, fixed directly at the entry point' and two jets 'only 100 feet apart, were forced to take evasive action.' The squadron filed a safety report. Graves's testimony records the institutional response: 'there was no official acknowledgement of the incident and no further mechanism to report the sightings.' Two of the three DoD-released videos, GIMBAL and GO FAST, both from January 2015, came out of this operating environment, and Tim Gallaudet's account of a recalled January 2015 Fleet Forces Command safety message citing 'multiple near-midair collisions' describes the command-level reaction to exactly this squadron's problem.
